processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Casting ingot homogenized at 1100 °C for 2 hr.
Hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800 °C followed by air cooling to room temperature.

Hot forged samples hot rolled (soaking 1100 °C, 2hr) in 1050-800 °C in two passes with 50% thickness reduction each pass, reheating at 1100 °C for 5 min between passes, finally water quenched from finish rolling temperature (~800 °C). Surface machined to 3 mm sheet.
Hot rolled & quenched 3 mm sheet intercritically annealed at 750 °C for 30 min, followed by air cooling to room temperature. Designated IA750_30 Min.

structures.overall_structure: Dual/multi-phase structure of stable δ-ferrite, untransformed austenite, reverted austenite (needle morphology), and intercritical ferrite (α) after intercritical annealing at 750 °C for 30 min; the δ-ferrite morphology remains unchanged from the HRQ state; fraction of reverted austenite decreased compared to IA750_5 Min due to dissolution into intercritical ferrite.

phases_present.morphology: island-like, structure/morphology unchanged after intercritical annealing; highly stable

structures.overall_structure: Austenite volume fraction measured by Rietveld refinement of XRD of the IA750_30 Min specimen.

interfaces.phase_evolution: In the IA750_30 Min specimen the fraction (area fraction) of reverted austenite decreased compared to IA750_5 Min, indicating dissolution of reverted austenite into intercritical ferrite (α-ferrite); with elemental partitioning Mn (and C) diffuse into adjacent untransformed austenite. δ-ferrite remains highly stable with no significant change in elemental distribution.
interfaces.interface_notes: APT/HRTEM interface analysis (enrichment of Mn and C, depletion of Fe and Al at the intercritical ferrite / reverted austenite interface) was performed specifically on the IA750_60 Min specimen, not IA750_30 Min.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8/E8M subsize tensile specimens machined by wire EDM along the rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: At least three samples tested, average values reported.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering and true stress-strain curves shown in Fig. 6A1 and Fig. 6A2 (IA750_30 Min curve, red).

strain_hardening_rate.value: mean work-hardening rate in stage S2 between 1700-1000 MPa
strain_hardening_rate.note: WHR curve of IA750_30 Min shown in Fig. 6B2.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: PSE = product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation.
Austenite volume fraction before/after tensile by Rietveld analysis of XRD; K by Sugimoto's model (eq 5).

characterization_methods.technique: Field Emission Gun Scanning Electron Microscopy (FEG-SEM) with Energy Dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS VP 300 FEG-SEM equipped with EDAX; at least 5-7 areas and 15-20 spots for elemental mapping of each phase, average with standard deviation reported
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM images at ~10 µm (low mag) and 2 µm (high mag) scale; EDS spectrum 0-9.00 keV
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate microstructure/morphology and elemental analysis of individual phases in the IA750_30 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS (Fig. 4B3): δ-ferrite Al 5.76±0.01, Mn 6.95±0.03 wt.%; reverted austenite Al 4.77±0.18, Mn 8.21±0.24 wt.%; intercritical ferrite Al 5.71±0.05, Mn 6.26±0.15 wt.%. Band of needle-like reverted austenite observed; no significant change in δ-ferrite elemental distribution.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 advanced XRD with Co-Kα (1.79 Å) target, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 20°-120°
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RT; before and after tensile testing
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases and quantify austenite volume fraction of HRQ and annealed specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite fraction of IA750_30 Min ~40% (before tensile), reduced from that of IA750_5 Min, confirming dissolution of needle-shaped reverted austenite into intercritical ferrite.

characterization_methods.technique: Work-hardening rate analysis from tensile stress-strain data
characterization_methods.purpose: Assess deformation stages and TRIP contribution
characterization_methods.key_findings: WHR curve of IA750_30 Min (Fig. 6B2) shows two stages S1 and S2; mean WHR in stage S2 between 1700-1000 MPa, higher than IA750_5 Min, consistent with increased UTS and TE.

characterization_methods.purpose: Examine fracture mode of IA750_30 Min specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: IA750_30 Min shows quasi-cleavage fracture surface with elongated ridges; δ-ferrite labelled; fracture predominantly cleavage due to high δ-ferrite fraction.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fraction vs temperature; duplex δ-ferrite + austenite region estimated ~650 °C to ~1350 °C; equilibrium austenite composition at 750 °C: Al 4.39%, C 0.47%, Mn 11.16%, Si 1.09%
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Intercritical annealing temperature of 750 °C chosen based on Thermo-Calc duplex region; correlated with dilatometry critical temperatures.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Variables: grain size (assumed finer austenite grain, 40 µm), temperature, alloy composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Theoretical SFE of designed steel ~35 mJ/m²; for IA750_60 Min reverted austenite composition SFE computed ~27 mJ/m², lower than equilibrium-composition SFE.

analytical_models.model_note: Theoretical SFE of designed steel ~35 mJ/m².

unmapped_findings: IA750_30 Min: nano-hardness was not reported for this specimen; Table 2 nano-hardness covers only HRQ, IA750_5 Min and IA750_60 Min (Fig. 5).

IA750_30 Min: after tensile test the austenite fraction decreased from ~40% to ~37% (Fig. 7c bars 40/37); K (mechanical stability) for IA750_30 Min ~1.10 (Fig. 7c label 1.079), suggesting relatively higher mechanical stability.

IA750_30 Min: fracture surface exhibited quasi-cleavage mode (Fig. 11d, 10 µm scale bar) similar to other annealed specimens; intercritical ferrite may contribute cleavage mode while reverted austenite may be responsible for dimples (ductile).

IA750_30 Min: elemental partitioning was not significant after 5 minutes of annealing, and it showed similar trends till the 30-minute annealing with only a slight increase in UTS and TE observed (b0046).
For IA750_30 Min the reverted austenite needle morphology persists as a band (Fig. 4B2); δ-ferrite fraction/morphology unchanged (highly stable δ-ferrite) relative to HRQ.

Theoretical SFE change: in IA750_60 Min, with Mn 7.58±0.14 and Al 3.96±0.15 in reverted austenite, SFE calculated ~27 mJ/m²; change of C to ~0.05 wt% lowers SFE to ~2 mJ/m² (thermodynamic Olson-Cohen model) — noted for the alloy/sample series, not specific to 30 min.
